title: Cross-Level Semantic Transition
holdout_rationale: The stage scopes were authored after the first cumulative-intersection failure. They test the proposed stage-reset operation and are not confirmatory held-out evidence.

research_intention.hypothesis: Explicitly governed stage-local constraint scopes can carry an interpretation from one resolved semantic region to another while retaining the earlier region as provenance, whereas flat cumulative conjunction can remain unsupported.
research_intention.primary_question: Can an interpretation transition from one semantic level to another as qualifying context is added, or does the current direct mechanism only perform flat conjunction?
research_intention.evidence_boundary: This synthetic operation experiment tests authored stage scoping. It does not infer legal causation, validate typed transition relations, establish facts, or determine a real legal conclusion.

cross_level_probes.description: Resolve an access-level qualification, then scope the evidential stage without retaining access as a final-target property.
Resolve opaque profiling, then qualify the dispute-level consequence under a stage-local scope.
Resolve recording transparency, then qualify the same recording as an evidential record.
